subject: Art & Design
title: Custom Corporate Typefaces: When Brands Design Their Own
description: A 60-second lesson on Custom Corporate Typefaces: When Brands Design Their Own.

hook.text: Netflix spent years designing 'Netflix Sans.' Not for beauty — to save millions in licensing fees.

buildup.text: Major brands commission custom typefaces: Apple (San Francisco), Samsung (SamsungOne), Airbnb (Cereal).

discovery.text: A custom font ensures no competitor shares your visual voice. It's as unique as a fingerprint.

twist.text: The ROI is real: licensing Helvetica across a global company costs millions yearly. Custom fonts pay for themselves.

climax.text: These typefaces are designed for specific needs: readability on tiny screens, consistency across 100 languages.

punchline.text: When your company is big enough, even the font becomes branded.

quiz.question: Why do major brands commission custom typefaces?
options: To save licensing fees and create a unique visual identity
Because existing fonts don't work on their devices

details.summary: Major brands commission custom typefaces — Apple's San Francisco, Google's Product Sans, Netflix Sans — to create unique visual identities and avoid licensing fees at scale.
details.whyItMatters: Custom typefaces represent typography's highest level of brand expression. When a company's text itself carries brand identity — not just the words, but the shapes of the letters — typography becomes the brand's most pervasive visual asset.
takeaways: Major brands commission custom typefaces for unique identity
Custom fonts avoid licensing fees and ensure consistency
They make the letterforms themselves carry brand personality

faq.question: How much does a custom typeface cost?
faq.answer: From $50,000 for a basic family from an independent designer to over $1 million for a comprehensive multi-script family from a top foundry. The investment is justified at scale — a company using a licensed font across millions of documents, products.

faq.question: Why did so many brands create custom sans-serifs?
faq.answer: Netflix, Airbnb, Google, Apple, IBM, and Samsung all created custom sans-serifs between 2015-2020. Beyond unique identity, these replace expensive Helvetica or Gotham licenses.
